_: Every threshold this plugin acts on, in one place. Read it; never repeat a number from it.
_provenance: Boot budget chosen by the row-S0 A/B, 2026-09-14: 81 cells (3 budgets x 3 loads x 3 curves x 3 seeds) simulated to day 365 through the plugin's own hooks. Run: eval/simulator/run.py --ab 20000,25000,40000 --horizon 365 --seeds 3. Result and reasoning: the repo's .orchestration/review/complete1-build-2026-09-14/ROW-S0.md.
_boot_budget_bytes: The @-import chain a session boots with. What the A/B established: 40,000 is ruled out (it costs ~2,762 more boot tokens every session for a boot-recall gain under the measured noise floor), and between 20,000 and 25,000 the instrument could NOT separate the arms in any load — its headline metric was DEGENERATE, reducing to 1/tokens, so it would name the smallest budget on any ballot and decides nothing by itself. The tie-break is the one piece of DOCUMENTED guidance that applies to this mechanism: Claude Code targets 'under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file', because longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. At the 101 B/line measured across real role files that is ~20,200 B, so 20,000 is the budget that guidance names.
_boot_budget_bytes_correction: This was 25,000 until 2026-09-14, justified by the auto-memory cap of 'the first 200 lines or 25 KB'. That justification was WRONG and the vault's owner caught it: that cap governs MEMORY.md only. The docs are explicit — 'This limit applies only to MEMORY.md. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length' (Claude Code docs, memory.md). This plugin's vault loads through @-imports from CLAUDE.md, which are never truncated, so no 25 KB cliff exists here and nothing was being bought by sitting under one. The real cost of a large boot file is context and adherence, not truncation — which is what the 200-line guidance is about, and it points at 20,000.
_boot_budget_warn_bytes: Warn on the edit that crosses this; refuse growth only past boot_budget_bytes. A door that first speaks at the moment it refuses has never given anyone a chance to act.
_compaction_floor_share: Compaction stops once the boot chain is at or below this share of the budget, rather than emptying the file. Measured against what our own boot-file graduations achieved (0.1-0.6).
_role_soft_limits_lines: Per-role line counts above which a file is offered to a cleanup pass. They are REVIEW thresholds, never delete thresholds, and a role absent from this table has no line limit. A stem here that the vault does not use costs nothing.
_boot_budget_warn_lines: The documented guidance in its own units. Kept in LINES as well as bytes because that is how the guidance is written, and because bytes-per-line varies by more than 2x across real role files (76 to 159 B/line measured) — a byte budget alone silently means a different number of lines in a terse file than in a discursive one.
_max_searchable_file_bytes: recall.py will not look inside a file larger than this, and says nothing when it skips one. Row S0 measured what that does: at medium load, day 365, 46% of held-out answers were already unreachable by tool call, and at high load 100% were -- because the rolling window pours every compacted entry into ONE growing archive file that crosses this ceiling. The number is here so a later row can read it rather than rediscover it; the fix is a SEGMENTED archive (row R3), not a larger ceiling.
_max_memory_file_bytes: The largest any memory file is allowed to become — a live role file is COMPACTED once it passes this, and an archive segment is SEALED and a new one opened before it would cross it. ONE number for both, because they are one rule: no memory file grows to where the search stops reading it. Deliberately a QUARTER of max_searchable_file_bytes — the margin is the point, not the equality, since a file allowed to sit AT the search ceiling is one oversized append from the cliff, and the failure is silent: the file simply stops being searched. Row R3, on row S0 measured at year 3: tool recall 0.00 at high load with Aporia.md at 7,001,112 B, Canon.md 6,887,434, Errata.md 6,807,646 and Patterns.md 6,872,157 — all LIVE files, none of them archives.
_triggers: OR semantics: any one arm firing is enough. Ported from the vault Stop hook's sections 3 and 5 by row R1, which reads them from here and holds no copy.
